utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, you've remembered.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: At this time, I have remembered, Your Honour, and I bring the matter of the motion that the Prosecution filed yesterday to your attention at this time because I'm afraid that in a few more minutes I won't remember anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. I think it may be convenient if we deal with the evidence of the witness first and then come to the motion. As I understand, there are one or two other matters as well. So if we can turn our attention to the witness in hand. Now, Ms. Motoike. May I remind you, sir, that the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence still applies.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, you indicated in pages 12 through 15 of your consolidated statement that you were taken to a location called Brace's house, and while there you saw Ljube Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that the witness be shown a clip, which is Exhibit P21, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, do you see the clip before you?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Do you recognise the persons depicted in this video clip?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And who do you see in this video clip?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ljube Boskoski and his body-guard.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And could you please identify or describe for us the clothing that you see Mr. Boskoski wearing?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is wearing black civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And could you describe for us the location of the body-guard that you've identified?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I see it on the video clip, he is on the left-hand side, the body-guard; while the other person is on the right.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could now show, please, Exhibit P46, which I believe has been admitted under seal. It bears ERN 0463-8823 in both the English and Macedonian versions. I'm sorry. It bears ERN 0463-8823. It was previously 65 ter 10.24. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, do you see the Macedonian version of this document?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Do you see, in the upper left corner of this document, it says, "Ministry of Interior, OVR Cair," and it's dated 12 August 2001, Skopje?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And the title is entitled "Certificate," and in the middle there, in bold, and it says, "On temporary seized possessions." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And right after, "On temporary seized possessions," it says: "On day of 12 August 2001, at the PS Mirkovci from the person," and it mentions Ramadani, Osman. Is that the statement that follows?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And later on in that same sentence, it says: "The authorised person," and there's a blank, "seized the following possessions in temporary custody." And on line number 1, it says: "One frame for AP (automatic rifle) calibre 7.62 with 18 bullets." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. These are all lies, misinformation. I never spoke about these things. I was a simple civilian. They took me from my own house.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. At the bottom left corner of the document, do you see a signature line, and it says: "Possessions were seized of," and there's a name. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Down there, the signature? Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: In the left corner, there's a signature. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is, but I was forced to sign. They did not allow us to read the document first. We didn't know what we were signing. We were supposed to sign blank papers.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And do you recall who forced you to sign?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't, because they were all wearing masks and my head was also covered, and I was not allowed to look up. But the accused must know who did this.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Do you recall if these persons were wearing uniforms?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know who killed them.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, if you could just answer my question. What I'd asked you was if you saw whether or not these persons who forced you to sign this document were wearing any uniforms.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: With uniforms and balaclavas.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: What kind of uniforms did you see on these people?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Different police uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could go on to another document, which is also P46 under seal. It was previously 65 ter 10.36. It bears ERN 0463-8843-N0463-8845, and the Macedonian version bears the same number.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please enlarge?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, give us a second. I think we're still trying to pull the whole document up. Okay. Can we go to page 1 of both documents, please. I have 14 hard copies. If I could assist, I could distribute those. Oh, there we have it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, do you see the Macedonian version of this document?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And I believe I forgot to ask you whether or not you read the Macedonian language.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Do you see, on the first page of this document, this is a document where at the top there's a name, "Ramadani, Osman"? Is that your name?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And right above that is a date, "14 August 2001," and there's also, below your name, a few words, "Velce Pancevski, Dobre Efremovski, Rumena Kostadinova." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could go to the second page of the document, both versions please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, do you see there -- I have a few questions about the contents of this second page. Do you see where it says "1605 hours" in the top of that page, and it says: "Started at 1605 hours."

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: It says: "Started at 1605 hours," and then in that paragraph that follows, the second paragraph, it says: "Advise pursuant to Article 210, paragraph 2, from ZKP, the accused was informed," and then it says: "was informed about a request under XXXIIKO," and there's a number there. There is a date, and it says: "on enforcement of investigation with the proposal to impose detention," and then the sentence follows, it says: "because of the well-based suspicion, he committed a criminal act of terrorism pursuant to Article 313 from ZKP." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Have you everyone committed any acts of terrorism?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not. It was never on my mind to do such things. As I said, I was an ordinary family person.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: But at this time, according to this document, you were accused of such conduct; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is right, but I was forced to sign these documents because they put this condition, "You're over if you don't sign."

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If you could look at paragraph 3 of that same page, the very last sentence, it says: "The accused stated, 'Today, I am brought here before the court, before the investigative judge, and I was beaten up by the police in reasons of the incident that happened on Sunday, 12 August 2001.'" Do you see that the last sentence of the third paragraph?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could go to page 4 of the English and page 3 of the Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: In the Macedonian, the second paragraph, last sentence, which is on the English, it's page 4, paragraph 3, it says: "Otherwise, I have wounds on my nose, head, and my forehead, also on my upper lip and all over my body. I need medical help." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and that is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And the other statement I showed you with respect to being beaten up, is that also a true statement?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, it is. I was brutally beaten up.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Can we go to the bottom of page 3 in the Macedonian version. I'm sorry. Yes. It is the bottom of page 5 in the English version. I think a different document has popped up on our English screen. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, at the bottom of the page there in the Macedonian version, do you see, in the middle, where it says: "Accused"?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Is that your signature there underneath the word "accused"?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if we can go to page 2 in the Macedonian version and page -- it only appears on page 2 of the Macedonian version. Could we, please, perhaps scroll over so the left margin of this document is showing, the Macedonian version.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Do you see there is a name or signature in the left margin of that document? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Motoike. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Ramadani.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, I am Edina Residovic, and together with my colleague, Guenal Mettraux, I am the counsel for Mr. Ljube Boskoski. Mr. Ramadani, you already gave some data on you, but I would like to ask you a few more questions to verify those. Tell me, is it correct that you were born on the 12th of May, 1966, in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you have spent all your life in Ljuboten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: There were seven children in the family; two brothers and four sisters?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In 2001, your mother was no longer living; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. My mother still lives.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, then I was misinformed.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise to you as well. Just put the questions correctly to me, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In 2001, you had your own family; your wife and three children. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You had by then completed secondary education, but at that time you were out of job. You were involved in farming; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The first statement you made was the statement to the OSCE; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also discussed with the representatives of the International Committee of the Red Cross; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As the distinguished colleague Prosecutor put it to you already, you have had several interviews with the investigators of The Hague Tribunal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Whenever you would have an interview with the investigators of the Tribunal, you would have an interpreter for the Albanian language; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You would sign, yourself, each and every one of your statements?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And whenever you were giving a statement, you stated that you are telling the whole truth to your best -- to the best of your recollection; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have told the truth, and I was there when whatever happened happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday, my learned colleague showed to you the consolidated statement and the corrections that you have made to the Prosecutors of this Tribunal, but you were giving your previous statements in your village of Ljuboten. It was always the case, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that it was customary to have several people interrogated at the same time, at the same time as you?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please? I'm not clear about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether it is correct -- or could you tell us, in your own words, whether on the day when you were interviewed, there were other people from Ljuboten interviewed with you together?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, those who went through it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, but the question, I think, at least as far as the interpretation, was a little confusing as to the manner or whether or not they were interviewed together in one place or "together" meaning in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I thought the question was fairly normally framed and would normally have elicited a sensible answer. Whether that answer might clear the distinction you are putting, I don't know, but the answer at the moment that we have received does not enable us yet to know what's going to happen. So please carry on, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Mr. Ramadani, was your liaison to the investigators of this Tribunal Mr. Kenan Salievski or Kenan Saliu?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I don't know who did what. I told the truth, and I'm very proud that this day came for me to be able to tell the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that you will also answer this as truthfully. Is it correct that you never received personal, at your home address, a summons from the investigators of the ICTY, but you were also informed by Mr. Salievski; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, they contacted me directly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your statements given previously, you were asked about your village and about any presence of the NLA in the village. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, of course, but what you are putting to me in your question is not true. They were all unarmed civilians and defenceless civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will ask you, Mr. Ramadani, to listen to my question and to answer my question. I never suggested -- I was never leading you in this respect. I only asked you whether the investigators who had interviews with you earlier also asked about the presence of the NLA in the village.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Ramadani, that you, as well as other citizens of Macedonia, knew through the media that in 2001 there were terrorist attacks against police stations taking place, as well as police patrols, military facilities, et cetera? Did you have such information in your possession?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there, I was living there, and I am a citizen of that state.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So if I understand you, you then had those information.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Ramadani, that some of the Albanian population in Ljuboten had affection or were supporting the actions that the NLA was engaged in?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, Ljuboten had nothing to do with it, and there was no NLA in our village. We didn't have any links with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that one part of the younger people from Ljuboten joined NLA directly and participated in their activities, then you could confirm that this is correct? Can you confirm this?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about what you are putting to me. I am talking only of what happened inside the village. Whether there was or there wasn't what you are telling me, then bring people here to prove that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you only about what you know, and I'm asking you to answer truthfully to what you know.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can ask me only about what happened in the village, please. Don't ask me anything that has to do with things that happened outside the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask, Your Honours, that we move into a private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My learned colleague showed you today the statements that you gave to the investigating judge. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Exactly. The judges, like the one that have taken the statement from you, were those in charge of carrying out the investigations in Macedonia. As a citizen, you must be aware of that; is that so?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware, but they didn't carry out any investigation in our case. Even the police and the judges should be held responsible for the crimes committed against us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your statements, you also saw that the Prosecutor was always present; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as a citizen of the Republic of Macedonia, you are aware that the Prosecutors, when they hear about something happening, they propose the course to initiate an investigation. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You explained, and you've mentioned that in the corrections that I put to you a while ago, that when you were by Brace's house, that then you saw Mr. Boskoski behind the wall that is between the street and the house of Brace; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you have said in those corrections, you've only seen the upper part of Mr. Boskoski's body?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, because you could not look up.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your earlier statements, I will mention the one from the 24th of October, 2003, you said that: "I've seen him before that many times on television. I believe it was at least three or four times. I didn't see Boskoski in the newspapers because I very seldomly read the papers. I'm not sure when was that he became a Minister, but I think that he was appointed a Minister when the previous government took power two years before the 2001 events." Do you remember saying this to the ICTY investigators?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that, describing Mr. Boskoski at that time, you have said that he was wearing civilian clothes, and then you have added: "I recall now that he was wearing some kind of a hat or a cap on his head"?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm absolutely clear that he was wearing civilian clothes, and this is what I said in my statement. He was not wearing any hat. Maybe it was a mistake by the interpreters, because I didn't see any hat. I only described what I saw him wearing.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So if that is written in your statement, which is 65 ter number 1D68, page 1D0848, in the middle of the text, then, as you are saying today, that must have been a mistake in the interpretation of what you were saying; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the corrections given to the Prosecutor in April 2007, you say that you've also seen Mr. Boskoski's body-guard called Goran?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I think this first page does not match the second page. There must be some mistake in what I've read, because the first page, the English page, is not at all the page I was talking about. But since I've asked the question and the witness responded to those questions, I think there's no use wasting time looking for the page of the transcript that would match this. So these documents could be taken off the e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, in the changes and additions that you have given, you have said that you've also seen Mr. Boskoski's body-guard and that you are sure his name is Goran; and then on the 8th of May, you arrived in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You've said that you recalled and that his name is Blagoje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not true that I recalled his name later. I worked in bit Bit Pazar. He was there. I would meet him very often, and I can recognise him very clearly, even from 100 kilometres distance, because I was involved in that tobacco business and I used to sell tobacco to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the questions of my learned colleague yesterday, when Mr. Boskoski's photograph was shown to you, together with his body-guard, if I remember well - I can't really quote - you probably said that it must be the mistake of the interpretation when "Goran" was written down instead of "Blagoje"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The interpreter was not that good, and I guess he did not understand me. I have known this person for 15 years. He used to work in the Bit Pazar police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct, Mr. Ramadani, that while staying in the Mirkovci police station, the medical officers have arrived twice at the call of the police to examine you?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After they completed two police shifts, after they carried out this beating and torture, this is how they treated us. It didn't look as serious behaviour to me, their behaviour towards defenceless civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Finally, is it correct, Mr. Ramadani, that the police called the ambulance to take Atulla Qaili to the hospital, and then on the next day, to transfer several more wounded prisoners; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you were not taken to the hospital at that time but that you were taken to the court, where you gave the statement; and after that, you were transferred to the Shutka Prison; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that a few days after being arrested, due to the appendicitis, you were taken to the hospital and there was a surgery performed over you?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you, you as a Defence representative, that this was not the reason why I was hospitalised. The reason was that I was seriously beaten. You should be ashamed to ask me questions of this kind. I was not there hospitalised because of appendicitis. I was there because I was beaten. We are here to tell the truth, and you, personally, I don't know where you lived at that time, in Croatia or in Bosnia, you received information which is not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, is it correct that you were given an appropriate medical assistance, you've been operated, and then you remained in the hospital until you recovered?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. They did what they wanted with me. I witnessed torture there as well. I was hit there, too. I don't know who hit me. I was hit and beaten up in the hospital as well. They kept me there as long as they wanted, two or three days. There were no rules.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Ramadani, that after you were released from the remand upon being pardoned by Mr. Trajkovski, by President Trajkovski, you never filed any criminal charges against the persons ill-treating you in Ljuboten, in the prison, in the Shutka Remand Prison, and in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But let me ask you: How can I press charges against them when they protect and defend a criminal, financially and otherwise? How can you file charges in a state that defends and protects perpetrators? This is quite impossible. I know what the rules are, but it was impossible for us to do it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, is it correct that you -- neither you nor anyone else from the village had no trust in the police and no trust in the Macedonian government, and that was the reason why you never pressed any charges against someone who ill-treated you?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true. How can you press charges against someone who actually killed members of your family, attacked your house? It was the state who should take the necessary measures to bring to justice what happened. If we really followed what the laws said, the law is not only for Macedonians. It should apply to Albanians as well, because Albanians have lived there for ages. They are indigenous people of that country as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Ramadani, is it correct that you, and all the others who were with you, trusted only the international organisations and that they spoke to them only, and it was only to them that they would give statements?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. When they released us, they should have come to our houses and asked what happened, and they should tell us that these crimes will be tried and justice will be brought.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But because of the great mistrust that you felt, you did not let the Macedonian police come to your houses and interview you about the events that took place; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, because we do not trust them because of what happened to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You didn't even want to discuss things with the Defence counsels of the accused, this year, the year before, for the same reasons? Even today, you're not prepared to discuss issues with the Macedonian police and the Macedonian authorities; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, no way. I would not discuss things with them in any way.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have a few more questions, but they are an entirety, so maybe it would be good to take the break now and then in the ten minutes after it I will finish my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will resume, then, at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, you surely remember that in April of 2002, exhumation of the bodies of the people who were killed on that date, 12th of August, 2001, was performed?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I was present there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But before that exhumation, representatives of the OSCE and representatives of the International Tribunal have had a meeting with the family members of the persons who were killed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Of course. A month before the exhumation started, representatives of the International Community; namely, OSCE and the International Tribunal, came to Ljuboten and had a meeting with the representatives of the families of the persons who were killed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask now that the witness is shown 65 ter number 1D83, 1D1143. I would like to ask that the table routed correctly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, we have here the names of the representatives of the families who were present in the meeting with the OSCE and the representatives of the ICTY. Before I ask further questions, could you recall or can I remind you and say that this meeting took place in the school of Ljuboten on the 8th of March, 2002?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not correct about the school.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The meeting you had before the exhumation took place?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understand you, I don't remember where the meeting was held. I know that there was a meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you look at this overview of names, in the penultimate place, the name "Ramadani, Osman" is written; and in the second column, "Relationship to the deceased," it says, "Son." Is that data yours, Mr. Ramadani? Were you the person present in the meeting?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I was present.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you were present as a representative of your family on the occasion of the death of your father, Muharem Ramadani; is that correct? Your Honours, considering that the witness verified the document, we seek to tender it as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D8 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to ask that the witness is shown the document 1D82, page 1D1140.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, this document was compiled by the representative of the ICTY, Howard Tucker. In relation to this document, I will ask you some questions. But before that, considering that the document is in the English language, I will read it to you so that you get the translation. In the document, at the very beginning, the word "Purpose" or the "Objective" of the meeting is written. It is written in the English language: "[In English] Meeting the representatives of the families of the deceased from Ljuboten, Republic of Macedonia to discuss the operational plan for the exhumation at the cemetery of the village of Ljuboten." Was the purpose of this meeting to discuss the exhumation of the bodies of the persons who were killed?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this part, where it states "Location," it says: "[In English] In Ljuboten, Republic of Macedonia." [Interpretation] So it took place at the school. Does this remind you that meeting took place at the school?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember. There were many such events. I do not remember that it was in the school, but it is true that we discussed this issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Because of the names that follow, I would like to ask that we move into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Ramadani, now we have here the third page of the notes compiled by the ICTY investigator, and I would like to show you the sentence in the seventh paragraph counting from the top, or the fourth one if we count from the bottom only, where the investigator says, speaking about his conclusion: "[In English] They still carry a huge mistrust of anything Macedonian." [Interpretation] Did the investigator convey your sentiment correctly, that you had a huge mistrust of anything Macedonian; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, I now seek to tender this document as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank you now, Mr. Ramadani, for answering my questions. Your Honours, I have completed the cross-examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit 1D9, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek that the document is received under seal, because it contains names of protected witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness, Osman Ramadani, will be cross-examined by my colleague, Jasmina Zivkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Zivkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Ramadani. My name is Jasmina Zivkovic, and together with my learned colleague, Antonio Apostolski, I am the Defence counsel for Mr. Johan Tarculovski. Mr. Ramadani, we heard yesterday from my learned colleague the Prosecutor, Mrs. Motoike, that you were born and you grew up in Ljuboten. I suppose that you have lived there all your life and that it is there where you completed your education. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, elementary school.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: And you received teaching in the primary school in your native language, the Albanian?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: You live with your family, with your wife and children, in the same house with your brother, Ismail Ramadani?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Today, you also told my learned colleague, Residovic, that you were selling cigarettes at Bit Pazar market; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I beg your pardon. Before the -- before the war, I was in Bit Pazar. Now I work as a farmer.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: And tell me, for how long were you involved in selling cigarettes?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you, ten to 15 years, but not with cigarettes but with tobacco producing.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: So then did you have a shop, a stall, for this Bit Pazar?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We sold it informally. This is where -- from this, someone can see how freedom we had. We were not even allowed to sell our own product.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ramadani, in your consolidated 92 ter statement of the 20th of April, 2007, P197, our number 2D2636, in the page 7, in paragraph 20, line 7, you say, and I quote: "I know that there was a certain number of villagers who were NLA members." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you clarify what is incorrect, that you stated this or that there were no villagers who were NLA members?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question? I do not understand the question because it seems as though there are two different questions in one. Could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. I will then repeat it. I quoted from your words, from your statement of the 20th of April, 2007, where you stated that you knew that a certain number of villagers were members of the NLA. My question is: Is it correct that you have stated this?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. I have not given such information in any statement of mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Do you know a person by the name of Ruhem Jashari, Mr. Ramadani?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He is a cousin of mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know his brother?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: In your consolidated 92 ter statement of the 22nd of April, 2007, P197, our number 2D2636, in the page 5, paragraph 11, line 6, you say, and I quote the question: "Was Ruhem a member of NLA?" And the answer is: "No. I know that his brother was a member of the NLA, but not Ruhem." Can you tell us, is this correct, that you have stated this?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it my statement? What has been said here, that his brother was member of the NLA, I don't think I have said that. They have put this here only to make me such a question. I was not interested in other people. I was only interested in my family, in what would happen with my family. I'm not interested in these kind of questions. My family never had any NLA members. We didn't even interfere or engage in such things.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, you say here, "They have put this just to ask me this question." Can you clarify, who put this to ask you a question, in order to ask you a question? Who is "they," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person that is asking the question has probably put that there; and if someone has said that I have given such a statement, he could just come and say that here. I was never interested in those things. I was only interested in my family. If I was such a family, I wouldn't be here now.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. I just read from your statement that you gave to the ICTY investigator.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I ask that not to ask me questions that have nothing to do with me. I want to be asked about questions related to what I have gone through.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. I just ask the question from something that you stated.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not a question for me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell me -- can you tell me, then, do you know the name of his brother?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is a cousin of mine. How could I not know my cousin? But it seems that someone knows better than I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: What is his name? Can you answer my question?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Orhan.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, were you ever a member of the NLA or another terrorist organisation?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do not make me such questions. I said that I wasn't. If I were, I wouldn't have suffered so much with my family, spiritual and all that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I am only asking you to answer my questions briefly so that we do not waste any time.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, make to me questions about what I have gone through. Ask me -- tell me who killed my father, who killed my cousins.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Ramadani, were you maybe a supporter, a sympathiser of NLA or any other terrorist organisation?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have had -- I have never had anything to do with all that, and I guarantee for my family 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Ramadani, in your consolidated statement, 92 ter(B) 197, our number 2D2636, of the 22nd of April, 2007, in the page 4, paragraph 5, line 3, you say: "I remember even today that on the Friday, two shells fell."

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: And then the boy, Erxham, was killed?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that it took place between 1700 and 1800 hours on the --

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know exactly the time. We had other things on our minds then than to look at the clock, but I am sure that it was in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter finishes the question: -- on the 10th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, before this court, your brother, Ismail Ramadani, stated that the boy was killed on the Friday morning. You do not agree with that, I suppose?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not agree. Maybe he looked at the watch. I just saw with my eyes that the boy was killed by the shell.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So if someone would say that the village of Ljuboten was shelled on the Friday morning, you would not agree with this?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not agree with heavy artillery, with automatic rifles. As a matter of fact, all this started as of 7.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Are we now talking about the 10th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: All right, thank you. All right, Mr. Ramadani. All the way until the Saturday evening, you were inside your house with your family?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I did not hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: And after that, you took shelter in the basement of your friend?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a friend; next of kin. He is not a friend. He is not a co-villager. We are relatives.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I suppose you were not able to leave the basement because of the shelling?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's normal. You know better than I. You just ask the question. She knows everything, what happened and how it happened. The criminals are here. They know what they did in that village. They know everything. You are just asking false questions. They are all false questions to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I have to ask you, again, to just answer my questions.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We couldn't get out. We couldn't get out because of the shelling. How do you think we could go -- we could get out?

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Tell me, while you were in the basement, you didn't have any communication with anyone from the village?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: How can we communicate when we could not get out of the yard?

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: So no one from among you had a mobile phone so that you could communicate and learn where the Macedonian security forces were located?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We knew where they were. They were deployed three months before the events around the village. We did not have any communication. Why should we have any communication? We were civilians. We trusted that nothing would happen to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I don't know whether you understood my question.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did understand your question, but your questions for me are misinformation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I would still like to ask you to answer my question again. Did someone from the people who were in the basement with you speak with the village inhabitants via a mobile phone on that day, 12th of August, the Sunday?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand. We didn't have such cellphones. They should tell that they have robbed us before getting us from the basement. There were other phones, but they were interrupted.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Land lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: In your 92 ter consolidated statement from 22nd of April, 2007, P197, 2D2636, page 10, paragraph 28, line 3, you say, and I quote: "The shelling stopped around 12.00, and then the army and the police entered the yard." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell whether the time is correct. It is correct that they entered, and it is correct that this is the way they entered: First, the army should and then they entered, the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I assume you saw the security forces through the window, the window to the basement where you were hiding.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We couldn't see them. If you were in my place, I would ask you if you could see them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you answer my question? Was there -- let me make it clearer. Was there a window in the basement?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a window, half a metre by half a metre. I would like to see a photograph. I would even want to see the people that were killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please recall and tell us, how many members of the security forces you saw at that time?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but she knows better than I. If she had her head covered as we had our heads covered, then we shall see if she can tell how many there were and if she could tell anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I did not get an answer to my question again.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you understood very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, please answer my questions. I wasn't there. You came here to tell the truth, and I believe that all us here would like to hear the right answers. Therefore, I would like you to explain and tell me, if you know, of course, and if you remember.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would ask the Counsel to avoid making me questions which, for me, are questions that serve to nothing, but I will try to answer. I could see something. My head was covered with clothes. I cannot exactly say how many they were. Here we have the criminals present. They know exactly how many there were.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. That means you don't even remember what kind of weapons they wore and what kind of uniforms they wore?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to ask of you, if we were allowed, as it is prescribed by law, to see them, but they have treated us as animals.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. So then the security forces members ordered you to go outside and to lay down on the floor -- INTERPRETER: Interpreter's correction: On the ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, what was the way that you were laying on the ground when you got out?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, but I have to use these words. We had to lie down as dogs.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, you left the basement through the door to the house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This question has no meaning, and I keep telling you that. You should ask me about what happened, exactly. You know very well what we used to get out. We went out through the half-metre-by-half-metre window, and they ordered us to go through this window. These accused know very well how we left that basement.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ramadani. Could you give me an answer to the previous question that I already posed but never got an answer to? Maybe we misunderstood each other. My question was to explain us in which way were you told by the security members to lay down on the ground in front of the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may inquire of the learned counsel, if this really goes to material issue, we've heard from other witnesses who have previously testified about perhaps some slight inconsistencies as to the manner in which they were laying down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I see no basis to interfere with the questioning at the moment, thank you. Carry on, please, Ms. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, once you got out, you were ordered to lie down on the ground in one row; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not lying down on ground. We were lying down on a concrete ground, and we were not lined up but we were lying down.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: You were all in one row?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please. I saw my brother there somewhere further up or further down. We were not allowed to see, and we were undergoing tortures. They were cursing us. It was impossible for us to see how many columns we were and how we were lying down.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ramadani, in your statement and additions and the changes, 92 ter P197 of 24th of April, 2007 -- I apologise, P198, our number 2D2447, page 4, paragraph 22, line 3, you thereby say: "I was able to hear -- I could hear Sulejman Bajrami running, and then I heard a shot." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I will tell you now. Sulejman was lying down, he was hit on his head, they forced him to walk ahead, and they shot at him.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. After that, you started walking towards Ljubanci; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. They made us take off our shoes. We were barefoot.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, were you followed by an armoured vehicle [as interpreted] on that occasion? I apologise. My question was plural, "vehicles." Maybe the interpretation was wrong.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two Hermelins entered the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. When you were walking towards Ljubanci, did you see any other vehicles, apart from those Hermelins that you just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When we were at Brace's house, they loaded us as if we were logs on this military truck.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: So except for the Hermelins and that truck, you saw nothing else on your path towards the Brace house?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already told you, we were not able to see. Our head was covered with T-shirts.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: And after some time, as you told us, you were transferred by a truck to the Mirkovci police station, and after some time to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not taken to hospital, but my relatives and my brother, they went to the hospital. Only a few of us remained there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ramadani. Tell me, are you familiar with the name "Commander Miskoja"?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, this is disgraceful. This "Miskoja," meaning mosquito in English, we keep our houses safe so that they don't get in our houses. I don't know where you get this term.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please answer to my question without commenting, please?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: But this is quite interesting, in fact, how they made a human being out of an insect, how they use an insect to refer to a human being.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the commander I asked you about, that he tried to enter the village of Ljuboten with his troops on the Sunday afternoon?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This has nothing to do with what happened. Whoever mentioned this person by this name, he or she should come here and testify if that is true or not. Please, Defence counsel, do not ask me questions based on misinformation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you. Mr. Ramadani, was the Basic Court Skopje II the one who released you for the acts about which there were charges pressed against you?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know very well how we were released. We were not released by the court. We were released by the president of the state, because he realised what were the real reasons why we were there. It says in the pardoning that we were allegedly something, but, anyways, "we will pardon you." They exactly what they wanted to do with us.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: So we couldn't agree that you were pardoned by President Trajkovski as an NLA member in accordance with the Ohrid Framework Agreement?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It looks like that, but we were not members of the NLA. We were presented as members just to facilitate our release and not --

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Ramadani. Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Zivkovic. Mr. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, you were asked about reporting the offences to the Macedonian authorities or police. Did any Macedonian police body or authoritative body ever try to contact you about the events in Ljuboten that you've described?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you for asking me this question. No, because it was these authorities who imprisoned us, who massacred us, who killed us, who tortured us, who beat us up. We ended up in prison. How could these authorities come and ask us these questions when they were actually satisfied why we were there and in that condition, although we were simple, ordinary civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, do you know if the Macedonian police or any authoritative body from Macedonia ever try to contact the village head in Ljuboten about the events?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was in prison, for this period, I cannot tell you. I cannot ascertain if this is true or not for this period of time, but personally I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: You mentioned a gentleman by the name of Goran, and you indicated that that person used to work at Bit Pazar police station. Can you tell us, how do you know that this person was a police officer in Bit Pazar?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know him very well, not only him but his family as well, because he used to serve his military service together with an in-law of mine in the JNA. So when I was selling tobacco in Bit Pazar, he used to work in this police station there.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: How was he dressed when he was employed with the Bit Pazar police station?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a normal police officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Normal police uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Can you describe the normal police uniform?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Normal clothes of the police, a blue colour. If it's warm weather, they would wear shirts; if it's cold weather, jackets. But it's a normal police uniform with the insignia, "Police."

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Could you tell us, if you can, could you tell us, where is Bit Pazar in relation to Ljuboten, as far as location?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's 12 kilometres from Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Motoike. You'll be pleased to know, Mr. Ramadani, that that concludes the questions for you. The Chamber would thank you for coming to The Hague and for the assistance that you've been able to give. You are of course now able to return to your home, and the Court Officer will show you out. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Perhaps this is a convenient time to look to the incidental matters, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The Prosecution has two matters to raise at this time. First of all, we would respectfully ask the Chamber whether it has had some time to ponder the Prosecution's motion that was filed yesterday to remove certain witnesses from its list. There are two persons named in that motion who are scheduled to travel here next week. One of those would be M-003 and the other would be M-004, and it would certainly be helpful to the Prosecution if the Defence could provide its position, and the Chamber as well, as to whether we might be able to cancel the travel of these two witnesses or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber has not heard anything of the position of the Defence, so it certainly has not formed views about this matter, Mr. Saxon. We can understand your desire to minimise unnecessary travel. We're also conscious, though, of the limited rate of progress through the anticipated witnesses. Almost without exception, the Prosecution examination of witnesses seems to take at least the time that has been estimated for the whole of the witness's evidence, including cross-examination and re-examination. So we are running slowly, and we are somewhat surprised to see the witness, M-021, who is listed for next Wednesday, is listed for only two hours, which would seem to us to be a noteworthy underestimate of what is likely. So I make those observations to point out that some of the problems that are being encountered are of the Prosecution's own making. I will now see if Defence counsel are in a position to assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. On a few matters, we can indicate at this stage that we will have no objection to the withdrawing of the first five thin witnesses mentioned on the application, which would include the two witnesses mentioned by my colleague, Mr. Saxon, if that assists the Trial Chamber. We would wish, however, to make further submissions in relation to the last of these witnesses, M-86. But before I do that, the Defence would indicate as well that the time which has been forecasted, so to say, for Witness M-21 seems to be an enormous underestimation of the time needed for this witness. I believe that his statement is 26 pages long and refers to many, many issues as well as many, many documents. So we would ask at this stage perhaps for the Prosecution to give another estimate, or at least we can give this indication to the Chamber, that we believe our cross-examination would be much, much longer than the estimate in question. If I may continue, Your Honour, on the Witness number 6, M-86. Your Honour will remember that last week on the 10th of May, a number of documents were presented to one Prosecution witness, M-17, and I can direct Your Honour to 643 to 654 of the transcript. At this time, Your Honour will remember that my colleague, Ms. Residovic, objected to two documents presented at the time. The objection at the time was essentially that the witness in question was unable to give evidence as to the manner or preparation of that document, of the circumstances of that document, and any other matter relevant to the reliability of those documents. Your Honour admitted these documents, however, and the Defence indicated that the witness in question would be coming as a witness to give evidence. Well, the author of one of these documents is the witness, who has now been withdrawn by the Prosecution, and the Defence is very, very concerned, Your Honour, about the request by the Prosecution. It seems, I insist, it seems to be the Prosecution case that this document is indicative of a sort of a nationwide joint criminal enterprise, in which a very large number of individuals, members of the Ministry of Interior or members of other institutions of the state, were involved in perhaps a wall of silence. Those accusations are pretty serious, and they are particularly serious if they are being made against a witness. Now, this witness, if withdrawn from the Prosecution list, will not get an opportunity to respond to this proposition, if that is indeed the proposition of the Prosecution. But more importantly for us, Your Honour, is the unfairness that is created to the defendant. Now we are faced with a Prosecution theory of the case based on documents which have not been presented to anyone capable of giving evidence of the whys of its content, the manner in which it was made, and the reliability of these documents, and we are unable to cross-examine a witness capable of giving that evidence. We have indicated, Your Honour, in the pre-trial conference, I believe, that we were concerned, to say the least, about the way in which the Prosecution case appeared to be sculpted. Your Honour had been told about an alleged sham investigation, but you will not see the president of that commission. You have also been told that there was no investigation in this case, but Your Honour will not hear about any Prosecution of any investigative judge who were involved in the investigation of this case. Now Your Honour is being told that these documents are evidence of a joint criminal enterprise and that a number of members of the Ministry of Interior were involved therein, but you will not hear from that individual. What the Defence proposes, Your Honour, or what we would wish in those circumstances, is for Your Honour to invite the Prosecution to call this witness. The Defence is not certain that Your Honour would have the authority to order the Prosecution to do so under the Rules, but we would respectfully ask that Your Honour be inviting the Prosecution to call that witness, so that this document can be put to that witness so that he can answer any suggestions or allegations which have been made about this document. We also believe that it would be very relevant and very important from the Court to hear, if you wish, the other side of the story, so that the truth of the matter, if that is the word, may be tested through this witness. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there anything you need to add, Mr. Apostolski?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I completely support the presentation of my learned colleague, so I would not like to repeat, and that's in the interests of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I would refer the Trial Chamber to a decision from the case of Prosecutor versus Halilovic, dated 7 February 2005, at page 6, where the Chamber held: "In principle, it is for each party to decide which witnesses to call to prove its case," and, "holding that Defence objections to Prosecution proposed withdrawal of witnesses was not justified." Your Honours, if there is a need for this Chamber to hear the other side of the story, to quote my learned friend, then that can be accomplished. If the Prosecution does not call a particular person, the Defence can call the person during the Defence phase of the case for any particular points they wish to show. The suggestion that the Prosecution has alleged a so-called nationwide JCE, in this case, is not only incorrect, it's also, if I may say so, inflammatory. My learned friend has told you that you won't see the president of a particular commission that was established to allegedly investigate the facts of this case. However, you will see at least two other members of that commission, gentlemen who are on the Prosecution's list of witnesses. Therefore, it's the Prosecution's position that it should be permitted to drop witnesses whom it no longer feels are necessary to prove its case, and any possible problem or concern caused to the Defence can be cured very simply. The Defence can call that person during their case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we've heard enough, Mr. Mettraux. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's a convenient reason for me to make a further observation unrelated to this application so that counsel are aware of it in future paper-dueling battles between them. Counsel may have noticed, in the last decision of the Chamber, we allowed leave to file a reply, which is a step beyond that which the Rules normally allow, but we did not allow a further reply and then a further reply to the reply to the reply. Counsel need to work out, at the beginning, what is the measure of their case on the issue, their point, and put it; then, unless there's been some significant surprise, there will be no need to reply because you will have dealt with the merits of your position. Leaving aside moments where people are genuinely taken by surprise, and that can occur, the Chamber will not be allowing these prolonged verbal battles to go on, taking a lot of energy and time and usually achieving nothing of great substance. We think it's going to be in the interests of the speedier completion of the trial and the more harmonious proceedings if counsel can confine themselves to the real merits in the first submission. Thank you for allowing me the opportunity to just add those little words. If you'll excuse us now for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon,, Witnesses 1 to 5 in paragraph 2 of your motion are not the subject of any dispute, and the Chamber grants leave for you to withdraw them from your witness list. The sixth witness, M-086, was a witness you, as I recall, intended to call primarily to produce a document. Admission of that document was not disputed on the basis of authenticity but was disputed on the basis of reliability. The Chamber, because there was no dispute as to authenticity of a document of a public nature from the records of the Ministry, admitted the document, but did indicate the issues of reliability would be able to be considered further in cross-examination as the witness was to be called. It's the view of the Chamber, in those circumstances, that fairness would require that we do not grant you leave to amend your witness list to withdraw the name of the sixth witness. Thank you. Now, was there any matter before we move to the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Following up on your encouragement of producing harmony between the Prosecution and Defence counsel, yesterday and also this morning there was a full and frank discussion between the Prosecution counsel and our colleagues regarding the need to move into private session, and there is now a consensus between the parties that, with the Judges' permission, the parties will no longer move into private session simply when they are referring to a particular individual or, for example, the name of the owner of a home, for example; instead, the parties will only try to move into private session when they need to refer to an individual and the fact that person will be a witness in this case. With your leave, that would be the proposed conduct for the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that, Mr. Saxon. It is, in fact, shall we say, a return to what is the appropriate position. But at the beginning stages of this trial, with everybody needing to become familiar with procedural issues and to become more familiar with what were the sensitive issues in the trial, it certainly was, I think, helpful, on the safe side, for there to be additional caution in the use of private sessions; that is, using them more than might really be justified. The important thing is that the viewing and listening public should not be aware that a protected witness is a witness. A fact that a protected witness is named in a neutral context in the trial creates no such understanding. If somebody is say, "On Monday at the shopping centre, I met six people," and names them, it says nothing about one of those persons being a witness in this trial. So the position that counsel have agreed upon is a very welcomed step. It's at a good time in the proceedings for us to move to that practice, and we encourage -- we both thank counsel for what they have done, and we encourage them to keep looking at any of these particular difficulties to see whether we cannot minimise them more, because the more we can minimise, the more smoothly and quickly the proceedings will flow. Could I mention, Mr. Saxon, that when you yesterday indicated that you wished to remove witnesses from the witness list, including two who were listed to be called next week, it was my first reaction that you probably would not need to try to fit any more in next week to replace the two that you were removing, partly because of the somewhat underestimation, on average, which I hope we will gradually be able to prove the estimation right by speeding up, but nevertheless at the moment we are not moving this quickly as the estimate; and, secondly, because of the witness M-21, which I think we can see will take time longer than the estimate. So you know more closely than we do, of course, but I think even with the two witnesses that are now removed from your list, even with those taken out of the schedule, I suspect we will be hard pressed to finish the remaining witnesses that you have listed for next week.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your point is well taken, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Very briefly, with the leave of the Chamber, Your Honour. Two very short matters. The first one has to do with a point of clarification. Your Honour has admitted a number of documents pursuant to the Prosecution application from the Bar table. The clarification we are seeking, Your Honour, is that a number of the documents which are included in this decision appear not to have been fully translated into English, and the point of clarification is whether Your Honours have admitted the documents in its entirety, pending translation, or only those parts that have been translated into English. The reason for our request, Your Honour, is yesterday we had to obtain a separate translation of a part which had not yet been translated. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
