utterances.text: In the course of a very large decision dealing with a great variety of exhibits, some of which had not been included in the motion, dealing with a document such as, for example, a court file, I think it became Exhibit 10 if I recall correctly --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters interfere: Could we ask the counsel to speak a little bit slower?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Counsel will comply. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And so will the Bench. We took the view, given the nature of that document, the fact that it was written in Macedonian, while conscious that the Prosecution, in its annex, had identified only certain parts of it, we admitted the whole document. The consequence is that there are some parts of it not formally translated. It is unlikely, from our rough judgement of the issue, that there will be anything material in the parts of the document that are not translated. But if it is the concern of counsel that one or more of the untranslated pages or documents within something like the court file is in fact going to be material, then we would suggest that that be taken up immediately with Mr. Saxon, and it ought to be possible to receive some attention to that individual document. We felt it important to have the whole file, but we did not feel there was justification in insisting on the whole file being translated when it is clear that quite a bit of it is merely procedural and is not going to impinge upon the merits of this case. So we must ask counsel, if they see a part of such exhibit that they feel is important, to then deal with that document individually to get translations.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We're grateful for this clarification, Your Honour. The last matter is a short, may I call pie for me, I hope it doesn't become a daily incident, but yesterday you will recall, Your Honour, that a document, or rather, an excerpt of a document was presented to a witness, Mr. Ismail Ramadani. The document was presented in such a way that Your Honour felt that it could have been misleading because of the way in which it was presented. I would wish to dispel any impression that there was any ill-intent in that regard. I would wish to indicate at this stage that we had not intended to use the document prior to cross-examination, and that I passed the document during the cross-examination to the lead counsel with the suggestion to use -- to put one proposition contained in this statement to this witness, and that perhaps I should have been more careful in explaining to lead counsel the where and the whys of this statement. Unfortunately, I didn't have the time to do that, so therefore, Your Honour, the fault was mine.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please, again, another request from the interpreters for Mr. Mettraux to speak a little bit slower. It is very difficult to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will again try my best the next time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Mettraux. Looking at the time, this is probably a good moment to have the break, and we can then resume and run through until 1.45. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And the next witness will be a witness in -- a protected witness, in case arrangements need to be made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And that will enable the court to be reset, yes. We will adjourn now, then, and resume at five minutes before 1.00.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please, again, another request from the interpreters for Mr. Mettraux to speak a little bit slower. It is very difficult to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will again try my best the next time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Mettraux. Looking at the time, this is probably a good moment to have the break, and we can then resume and run through until 1.45. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And the next witness will be a witness in -- a protected witness, in case arrangements need to be made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And that will enable the court to be reset, yes. We will adjourn now, then, and resume at five minutes before 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. Would you please read aloud the affirmation on the card.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if I could trouble you again. Take that piece of paper to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness, without stating your true name, do you see your true name written on that piece of paper in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And today, instead of addressing you by your name, I will address you by the number M-039. Is the other information on that piece of paper correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: It's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please show that piece of paper to Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note: The blind is up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And so, Your Honours, if you see me appear to be twitching to my left periodically, it's just that I'm trying to check where we are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's also the case that there is nobody in the public room.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if that piece of paper could be admitted into evidence under seal, we would be grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P199 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness, on the 10th of -- this is not a question, Witness. I'm just going to read a brief summary of your evidence: "On the 10th of August, Witness M-039" -- I should say: "On the 10th of August, 2001, Witness M-039 was beaten and mistreated at a police check-point, and his car was fired at by a police unit. On that day, a number of Ljuboten villagers fled to neighbouring towns, and at least one child was killed by shelling." I should say that, for the public, Witness M-039 was and remains a resident of the village of Ljuboten. "On the morning of 12 August 2001, M-039 and others sought shelter at the home of Mr. Xhelal Bajrami due to the heavy shelling. At around 2.00 p.m., screams and gunfire were heard from the direction of the Ahmeti or Ametovski house. Witness M-039 ran and hid close to the home of a man called Qani Jashari. Xhelal Bajrami, Bajram and Kadri Jashari sought shelter in the house of Qani Jashari. "Policemen arrived and fired at that house, and Witness M-039 later found the bodies of all three in a nearby field. When Witness M-039 last saw the three persons who died, these persons were not carrying any weapons. The Macedonian police burned a number of houses and destroyed property and livestock during the attack on 12 August 2001." I'd like to ask Ms. Walpita, we have copies of the 92 bis statements, is my understanding, is that correct, or at least one copy? There were two, were there not? There were two statements, please. Mr. Usher, if you could simply place these documents just in front of the witness, please, in case he needs to look at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness M-039, do you recall giving -- do you recall giving two statements to members of the Office of the Prosecutor about the events that you witnessed in Ljuboten village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And do you recall, in August of 2006, that your two statements were certified by an officer of this Tribunal; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And at that time, do you recall that you had the opportunity to review your statements in your native Albanian language?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And were the contents of your statements that you reviewed true and correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: True, true and correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender these two statements that have been certified pursuant to Rule 92 bis, please, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P200 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we briefly move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I do believe my efficient case manager has prepared some copies of the exhibits that I'm going to show this witness. If they could be distributed to the Judges. Well, what I just said was incorrect, Your Honour. If the witness can be shown, please, 65 ter number 199.9, and this is photo A on page 12 of your court binders, Your Honours. It has ERN number N004-4694. That is not the photograph that I'm looking for. I'm grateful to Ms. Greguric for her efficiency. That's fine, the photograph is fine now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness M-039, can you take a look at that photograph, please. First of all, can you tell us, please ?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Perhaps again I will need the assistance of the usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you please take the pen that's connected to the computer screen in front of you and draw a circle around -- no, let me start again, let me start again. Do you see the home owned by Qani Jashari on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you please take that pen and just draw a circle around that house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, maybe you could erase that little circle and draw a circle around the house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just the house. Thank you. Could you, please, to the right, just above that circle, just above it, could you write the initials "Q.J.," please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: In the middle or on the side?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just above, just above the circle that you drew.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Are you familiar with a compound of homes that belonged to the Ametovski family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could you mark an X above that home or homes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Witness M-039, roughly, roughly, how far would you say -- how far is the distance between the Ametovski homes and the home of Qani Jashari, in metres, approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure in metres. Maybe about 200 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Witness M-039, on the 12th of August, was there a time when you had to hide in some bushes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, or can you perhaps draw an arrow indicating more or less where you were, where you were hiding that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, below that arrow, could you draw the letters -- or the number "M-39"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. We see on this photograph, to the left of the number "M-39", we see four homes that appear to be completely constructed. On the 12th of August, 2001, had those homes been completed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Those homes had been completed and were fully constructed on the 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: The first two, from the outside, they were complete; maybe not from the inside, but the way you see them right now on the screen, this is the way that they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But there are four homes there. How about the other two? Were they all completed from the outside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: Yes, from the outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: From the inside, were they completed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: From the inside, two of these houses were not completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would tender this photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P201, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we could please look at Exhibit -- excuse me, 65 ter number 199.11, which is photo C on page 12 of the court binder. It has ERN number N004-4698.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness M-039, do you see this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And to save time, the house in the foreground, just to the right of centre, is that again Qani Jashari's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you please, above that house, write the letters "Q.J.," please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, again, can you please mark with an arrow approximately where you hid that day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And above those bushes, could you please write the number"M-39".

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. In that house, the house of Qani Jashari, we see two windows, one above the other. Do you see those two windows?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: On the 12th of August, 2001, did you see anyone use that window, move through that window?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Coming out of which of the windows? There's two of them there. The one on the top or the one on the bottom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: The one on the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you draw a circle around that bottom window, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, if there could be a redaction of an identifying word on page 67, line 5, that would be helpful. It refers to a familial relationship, the words (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness, can you simply tell us the names of the people who came out of that window? Nothing more about them, just their names.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: Bajrami Jashari, Kadri Jashari, Xhelal Bajrami.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When these three men came out of that window, were you able to see where they went or which direction they went?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: They came out of the window, then the house was on fire. There was a haystack. There was a lot of smoke, and I don't know what else.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And do you know, were you able to observe what caused the fire in the house and the haystack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: In the haystack, the Hermelin entered, and the haystack was set on fire; then the house was set on fire, and then I couldn't see anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could you observe who was causing these fires?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: This fire was set by the Macedonian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender this exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P202, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we could now please show the witness photographs from Rule 65 ter number 187.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness, do you see the photograph in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And what does this photograph depict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: The damages of the house and the way the house was burnt.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can you just -- just so the record is clear, whose house are we seeing there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: This is the house of Qani Jashari.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You see some handwriting below the photograph. Do you recognise your handwriting there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: This is my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you read what it says, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: "The damage caused to -- after the firing and after it was set on fire by the Macedonian police on 12th of August, 2001, in my presence."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this document, and I'd also like you to know that we have produced another copy of this photograph with the English translation of the Albanian words that you see at the bottom, and it's my understanding it is also in e-court. Perhaps our efficient Court Officer might be able to pull it up. That's it. Thank you very much. We can see it now, we can see the English translation on the right-hand side. Your Honour, I would ask that both versions of this photograph be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P203, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now, from the same 65 ter number, if we could please show the witness the photograph with the ERN -- and I'm momentarily confused because I am looking at two different ERNs on the same photograph. Let's try for N000-0892. And if that doesn't work, I have a Plan B. Let's try, then, N000-7826.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the first ERN?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The first ERN, N000-0892. Could you possibly look for N000-7826? That would be the ERN next in line from the previous exhibit. If our luck is not good, I have a hard copy of the photograph and we could plays it on the ELMO. That's it, our luck has turned, thanks to Ms. Greguric. Can we zoom in a little bit, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness M-039, do you recognise the person shown in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And what does this photograph show?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: Bajrami Jashari.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you know, at the time of this photograph, was Bajrami Jashari alive or dead?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: He was dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness, I know this is difficult for you. I'll try to move through this as quickly as I can. Do you see the handwriting at the bottom of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you recognise your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you please read to us what you wrote there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: "This photograph is the same -- it depicts the same position as I find it when they were killed."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Does it say "I found it" or "I found them" on the day they were killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: "This is the photograph that depicts the position, the way I saw him that day, dead."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we can also show the Chamber a copy of the same photograph that has the English translation of this comment. I'm sorry. I didn't see it. If that -- we can now see the English translation that has been done. Your Honour, I would seek to tender both versions of this photograph, please, into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There are more photographs in this group being tendered, are there not?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: One more, Your Honour, just one more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will give them -- they're all in one set on e-court, so we will give them one number.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Fine, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: When it comes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I do note that -- never mind, we'll move on. If we can now show the witness, please, a photograph also from 65 ter number 187 with the ERN number N000-7827. I misspoke before, Your Honour. There are two more photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness M-039, do you recognise the person in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Who is that person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: Kadri Jashari.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you know, when this photograph was taken, was Kadri Jashari alive or dead?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: Dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you recognise your handwriting at the bottom of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you read what you wrote, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: "This photograph depicts the same position of Kadri Jashari as the day when he was killed."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we could briefly show the version that has the English translation of that comment. Maybe we can just scroll down in this photograph. There we see it there. Thank you very much. If we could now turn to the last photograph, which is N000-7828.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: While we're waiting: Witness M-039, when you refer to the term "the day he was killed," can we agree we're talking about the 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That was the date when these gentlemen died; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we can enlarge this photograph a bit, please. Actually, we need to see the next photograph, N000-7828. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you recognise the person who we see in this photograph, M-039?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Who is this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: Xhelal Bajrami.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When this photograph was taken, was Xhelal Bajrami dead or alive; do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: Dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is that your handwriting at the bottom of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you read what you wrote, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039
utterances.text: "This photograph shows the position -- the same position of Xhelal Bajrami as the day when he was killed."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we could briefly just see the version that has the English translation, please. So, Your Honours, I would then seek to tender these photographs in the format that is most convenient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P203.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And I have no further questions at this time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Given the time and the difficulty for (redacted) I think this would be a convenient time to conclude for the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I believe we're in public session, Your Honour. I believe the name of the witness was just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It was. Sir, we must finish in a few minutes' time. The questioning by the Prosecutor has finished. Other counsel will want to ask you some questions, but there won't be time enough for that today. I'm sorry about that. It means that you will need to return on Monday to complete your evidence. So we will adjourn now, and we'll resume at 9.00 on Monday morning.
